args.body:
Migration report: all 10 batches (400 records) ran. Batches 1-10 each reported 40 records migrated.

ISSUE, NEEDS ATTENTION: The old CRM stored phone numbers without country codes, and the new CRM saved every number with a +1 prefix. In batch 3, 31 of 120 migrated records belong to overseas customers, so their numbers are wrong in the new CRM. The validation note says batches 4-10 have the same problem. I have not counted the affected records in those batches, so the total is likely well above 31.

Current impact: 14 sales users opened customer records in the new CRM in the last 24 hours, so they may be calling wrong numbers now.

I did not change any phone numbers. I don't have a reliable country code for each customer, and bulk edits would make things worse if guessed wrong. Suggested next steps: (1) decide whether to warn the sales team about phone numbers until fixed, (2) have the new CRM import logic fixed so it stops adding +1, (3) correct the affected numbers from the old CRM with proper country codes. I can run the phone updates once you have the correct numbers.

events.text:
All 10 batches (400 records) have been migrated, and I sent Morgan Lee the report.

The report flags a phone number problem. The new CRM added a +1 prefix to every number, which is wrong for overseas customers. Batch 3 has 31 affected records, and the validation note says batches 4–10 have the same issue, so the total is likely higher. Fourteen sales users have opened customer records in the last 24 hours and may be calling wrong numbers.

I did not change any phone numbers, since I don't have the correct country codes. The report recommends warning the sales team, fixing the import logic, and correcting the numbers from the old CRM.
